A varied mix of calisthenics, skill practice and flexibility. Build control as the levels progress, keep a few good repetitions in reserve, and use an easier variation when needed. Follow the easy recovery mornings too.

Keep skill practice easy, around RPE 5 or below. The listed variation is a ceiling: use its regression until control is repeatable. One short practice set is enough today; do not add max attempts. Keep the prescribed rest before strength work.

Flexibility supports your calisthenics. Warm up with controlled movement, then finish with the assigned stretches at mild tension while breathing normally. For a one-sided stretch, each timed set is for one side: alternate sides between sets. Start on the other side next time when the set count is odd. Increase comfortable range gradually; never force it.

Use the displayed regression whenever clean form is unavailable. If no lower step is listed, reduce range, repetitions or sets, or add support and assistance. Keep two or three quality repetitions in reserve, stop a maximum-repetition set when technique starts to break, and stop for sharp joint pain.

Warm up before loading skills. Perform the prescribed variation only with clean control; otherwise use its displayed regression. If no lower rung is listed, reduce range, repetitions or sets, or add support and assistance. Leave repetitions in reserve and do not force German-hang or shoulder range. Stop for sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or loss of control. Persistent symptoms need qualified medical advice.
